title: Invariant after Mutation
concept: Invariants are automatically re-checked after every mutation to the type's value — ensuring no operation leaves the object in an invalid state.
why: The most dangerous moment for any object is right after a mutation. Auto-checked invariants ensure you can never accidentally create an invalid value.
syntax_ref:
var x: InvariantType = valid_value;  // Checked
x = new_value;                          // Re-checked
x.field = value;                        // Re-checked
method(&mut x);                          // Re-checked after method
tips: After any mutation, ALL invariants are re-checked — you can't sneak an invalid state in
Use requires on mutable methods to bound the operation BEFORE the invariant check
The invariant check is the last line of defense — requires is the first
Don't rely on invariants alone for method preconditions — use requires for per-call validation
common_mistakes: Assuming invariants are only checked at construction — they're checked on EVERY mutation
Mutating an invariant type in a loop — invariant is re-checked each iteration
Not adding requires to mutable methods — the invariant catches the error, but later than ideal
